assumptions: The Linear webhook payload includes comment.id, comment.body, and comment.reactableId.
The Slack integration has access to the target channel and thread timestamp.
The GraphQL mutation for adding a reaction uses the comment's reactableId as the input ID.
Slack posting to a thread requires the parent message timestamp (ts) which will be derived from the Linear comment context or a configured default.

notes: Verify Linear-Signature header using webhook secret and raw body; reject if mismatch or timestamp skew >60s.
Webhook payload includes action, type, actor, data, createdAt, url, webhookTimestamp.
For comment.created: data contains comment fields id, body, issueId, userId, reactableId (if applicable).
reactableId is the comment's own ID for reacting to itself; confirm from Linear GraphQL schema.

example.query: mutation AddReaction($input: ReactionCreateInput!) { reactionCreate(input: $input) { success reaction { id type user { id name } } } }

notes: Uses Linear GraphQL API endpoint; authentication via Bearer token in Authorization header.
Mutation reactionCreate requires reactableId (comment ID), userId (actor), and type (reaction enum).
Refer to Linear GraphQL schema for ReactionCreateInput fields and ReactionType enum values (e.g., THUMBS_UP, HOORAY).
